clues.title: Bollard: Bollard
text: Ecuador is one of the countries in South America that uses bollards extensively, making them quite common in the country. There are two main types of bollards:
A round bollard with two red stripes
A flat bollard with two red reflectors on black
While other types of bollards can be found, they almost always follow the same color scheme and style.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Ecuador shitcam
text: If you have vibes that you are in South America and coverage was taken using "shitcam" camera you gonna be in Ecuador. There is "shitcam" in other countries but in South America you can only find "shitcam" in Ecuador.
Note: Ecuador also has GEN3(and little bit of GEN4) coverage not only shitcam! So don't discard Ecuador if it's not shitcam.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Atahualpa road
text: One road on the southern east coast of Ecuador looks a lot like a gray, dirty, depressing version of Tumbes or Piura, just with more garbage. It has an offshoot with a pretty beach.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Shitcam
text: Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Ecuador.
This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”).
It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours.
Within Latin America, Ecuador is the only country that has shitcam coverage.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Pole: Ladder Poles
text: Most poles in Ecuador are round and made of concrete.
These poles are fairly generic and not all that useful to identify the country.
**However, sometimes you will see another, more useful type of concrete pole: The ladder pole.**
It has a lot of small indents – resembling the steps of a ladder.
Within Latin America, these poles are more or less unique to Ecuador.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Stubby Antenna
text: All Generation 3 coverage is made with a white car, with a short and thick antenna (“stubby antenna”).
The antenna and or car are not always visible.
Mexico, Brazil and Colombia can also have this same short antenna.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Chevron: Chevron Spam
text: Ecuador often uses a lot of chevrons in road curves (“chevron spam”), usually considerably more than most other Latin American countries.
Colombia also occasionally uses a lot of chevrons in curves.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Plate: License Plates
text: The standard licence plates are white and can be short or long.
In street view, you will often see a mix of both sizes.
Commercial vehicles, such as taxis or buses, can have older solid orange plates, or newer ones with an orange bar at the top.
Ecuador is the only country in Latin America to use a mix of short and long licence plates.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guardrail: Double Guardrails
text: Double guardrails are very commonly used.
This is much less common in other South American countries.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Gen 4 Truck

The pickup truck in Panama has an antenna on the front.

clues.title: Architecture: Architecture
text: Most houses are made of grey bricks and have metal roofs.
This is not unique to Ecuador, but is very common.
Countries such as Peru, and especially Bolivia, commonly use red bricks.

clues.title: Landscape: Ecuador Dry Coast
text: This extremely dry landscape is only found in the coastal region between Guayaquil and Manta.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Guayaquil Flatland
text: The flattest region is located around the city of Guayaquil. This is most easily seen on the E-25 and E-48. The Amazon area is also very flat, and will be described below.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Ecuador Amazon
text: The Amazon area is very distinct. It is fairly flat, and contains many of these trees with white bark (Cordia trichotoma), and oil palms. The vast majority of the coverage notably uses the rarer “high antenna”.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Esmeraldas Landscape
text: The province of Esmeraldas can look similar to the Amazon region, but it is significantly hillier.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Southern Mountains
text: The southern regions have many winding mountain roads and exposed brownish red dirt. The central provinces can have similar roads, but the exposed dirt will usually not be found in these areas.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Chimborazo
text: The province of Chimborazo is semi-arid, and has an abundance of pine trees.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Galapagos Islands
text: The Galapagos Islands are an archipelago located west of mainland Ecuador. There are only trekkers and boat coverage on and around the islands. There is a wide variety of landscapes, including volcanic soil, low shrubbery, and craters.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Bollards
text: Ecuador is one of the few Latin American countries where bollards are very common.

A **round** bollard with two red stripes,
A **flat** bollard with two red reflectors on black.
